statusText: Mapped policy state: STRONG_BLOCK_NO_NEW_RISK. Fresh delayed NQ evidence remains strongly downside-efficient, with price still well below the session high and cross-asset pressure aligned.
recommendation: High Tail reflects observed persistent downside structure rather than event importance alone. A durable reclaim, deeper retracements and broader two-way rotation would support de-escalation; renewed fresh lows or shallow rebounds would preserve the restrictive state.
headline: Fresh NQ downside extension keeps Tail high ahead of the U.S. data and cash-open cluster.
body: At 10:36 UTC delayed NQ was 30,454.5, down 1.01%, versus a 30,370 session low and 30,713.5 high. Technicals remained Strong Sell with RSI 21.1, ADX 78.0, MACD -111.8 and negative Highs/Lows. U.S. 10Y was 5.126%, Brent 104.58 and VIX 16.13 (+6.26%). Shared Finviz context was stale and excluded.

lookbackSummary: Tail rose through the September 23 selloff, normalized overnight, then rebuilt from low/watch levels to high as fresh September 24 downside efficiency persisted. Prior hourly opinions are preserved from published history.
outlookSummary: Current high Tail is anchored to fresh persistent downside structure with aligned rates, oil and volatility pressure. The 12:30-15:15 UTC data/open cluster keeps Stress extreme; later Tail remains conditional on observed retracement quality and directional efficiency.

forecast.analysis: Fresh 10:36 UTC delayed NQ evidence shows 30,454.5, down 1.01%, with the contract still in Strong Sell. RSI 21.1, ADX 78.0, MACD -111.8 and negative Highs/Lows confirm persistent downside efficiency; a rebound from the 30,370 low keeps Tail below critical.

forecast.analysis: Into 12:00 UTC, Tail remains high only if the pre-data decline keeps producing weak rebounds or fresh lows. A sustained reclaim away from the session low would weaken the one-way-path case before the 12:30 UTC releases.

BEA international-transactions data and weekly claims are due at 12:30 UTC, with Hammack at 12:50. Stress is extreme; Tail stays high only if the observed post-release path extends directionally with shallow or failed retracements.

Into the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, high Tail is conditional on pre-market downside pressure carrying through the opening auction. Repeated extension, weak rebounds and session-extreme holding would sustain the restrictive state.

New Residential Sales is due at 14:00 UTC. High Tail is conditional on the actual open/data reaction remaining directionally efficient; broad two-way rotation or a durable reclaim would support de-escalation.

By 16:00 UTC, the opening impulse must remain unresolved to keep Tail elevated. Wider rotations, deeper pullbacks or fading volatility would reduce the probability of a prolonged mean-reversion failure.
At 17:00 UTC, elevated Tail requires the morning trend to retain directional progress. Full retracements of intraday extensions or a balanced range would argue for continued de-escalation.
At 18:00 UTC, the model assumes less path persistence unless new directional evidence appears. Residual one-way structure would keep Tail elevated; repeated two-way swings would lower it further.
By 19:00 UTC, WATCH-level Tail reflects residual trend risk rather than an assumed continuation. A late-session extension toward extremes would re-escalate risk; stable rotation would not.
At 20:00 UTC, the forecast favors a lower but still cautious state unless the U.S. session develops a second directional leg. Mean-reverting swings would keep Tail in WATCH rather than elevated.
At 21:00 UTC, persistent late-session trend pressure would keep Tail above the low band. A settled range and repeated retracements would reduce one-way-path risk.
At 22:00 UTC, Tail remains WATCH only if the closing sequence leaves unresolved directional pressure. A broad close away from extremes would support further normalization.
At 23:00 UTC, the forecast assumes the U.S. close no longer shows strong one-way efficiency. Any renewed extension into the futures reopen would invalidate that normalization.
At 00:00 UTC, low Tail assumes orderly overnight price discovery and no fresh geopolitical or rates shock. New directional gaps or failed retracements would lift risk.
drivers: Fresh geopolitical or rates shock risk

forecast.analysis: At 01:00 UTC, low Tail remains conditional on balanced overnight trade. Strong Asian-session alignment with rising yields or oil would be a re-escalation signal.
At 02:00 UTC, the baseline is normal overnight structure with meaningful two-way trade. Persistent fresh lows or highs without retracement would invalidate the low-Tail state.
At 03:00 UTC, low Tail assumes no sustained one-way Asian-session extension. Cross-asset stabilization would reinforce that view; renewed aligned pressure would not.
At 04:00 UTC, the forecast remains low Tail if Europe approaches without a fresh directional gap. A large gap with shallow pullbacks would raise path risk.
At 05:00 UTC, low Tail assumes European pre-open flows remain balanced. A renewed bond or oil shock combined with NQ holding at extremes would increase risk.
At 06:00 UTC, low Tail still depends on orderly European trade. Repeated extension after failed retracements would move the regime back toward WATCH.
At 07:00 UTC, WATCH begins to reflect increasing U.S.-morning sensitivity rather than observed future weakness. Any renewed one-way structure would raise Tail beyond this baseline.
At 08:00 UTC, WATCH-level Tail reflects proximity to U.S. morning catalysts while remaining conditional. Stable yields, oil and two-way NQ trade would limit escalation.
At 09:00 UTC, Williams is scheduled for a policy panel at 09:15 UTC. The event raises Stress; Tail would rise only if the observed market response becomes persistently directional.
At 10:00 UTC, WATCH persists ahead of later U.S. data. The score assumes no fresh one-way path yet; renewed trend efficiency or cross-asset alignment would raise Tail.

forecastDetail.comment: Current fresh delayed NQ evidence remains strongly downside-efficient, with aligned yield, oil and volatility pressure.
High Tail persists only if pre-data rebounds remain shallow or new lows appear; a sustained reclaim would weaken the case.
The 12:30 UTC data and 12:50 UTC Hammack remarks raise Stress; Tail depends on the observed post-release path.
Cash-open risk is conditional on continued directional efficiency, failed retracements or session-extreme holding.
New-home sales adds another checkpoint; no release result or market reaction is assumed in advance.
Elevated Tail after the opening sequence requires unresolved directional pressure rather than generic volatility.
